report.tagline: One of Europe's biggest takeaway apps, mixing restaurants that deliver themselves with orders delivered by its own couriers, now owned by Prosus.
report.simpleSummary: Just Eat is the takeaway app many UK families have used for years. You pick a local restaurant and order; sometimes the restaurant's own driver brings it, and sometimes a Just Eat courier does. It runs as Just Eat in the UK, Lieferando in Germany and Thuisbezorgd in the Netherlands. The Dutch-South African tech investor Prosus bought it for about £3.6 billion in 2025.

overview.whatItDoes: Just Eat Takeaway runs takeaway apps across Europe. It started as a pure marketplace where restaurants handle their own delivery and pay a small commission. Over time it added its own couriers so it could list restaurants like McDonald's that do not deliver.
howItWorks: Customers open the app and see local restaurants with delivery time, minimum order and fees.
In the marketplace model, the restaurant's own driver delivers and Just Eat takes a lower commission, around 14%.
In the delivery model, a Just Eat courier picks up the food and the commission is higher, often around 30%.
Customers pay by card or in some markets cash, and track the order in the app.
Just Eat+ members pay a monthly fee for free delivery on orders over a minimum.
Prosus is adding AI tools, such as better search and order predictions, from its other food apps like iFood.
overview.valueProposition: The widest choice of local takeaways, including small independents that only deliver themselves, all in one app.

businessModel.summary: Just Eat earns commission from restaurants and fees from customers. Marketplace orders cost little to serve. Delivery orders earn more commission but cost more due to courier pay. Prosus is focused on growing orders and profit through better tech.

revenueStreams.detail: Around 14% on orders the restaurant delivers.

businessModel.pricing: Commission around 14% (restaurant delivers) or around 30% (Just Eat delivers), plus a joining fee. Customer service fee and delivery fee vary. Just Eat+ is a monthly fee in some markets.
businessModel.unitEconomics: On a £25 marketplace order, Just Eat earns about £3.50 in commission plus about £1 in service fee, with little delivery cost. On a £25 delivery order, it earns about £7.50 plus fees, but pays a courier about £5. Marketplace orders often earn more profit per order. This is why Just Eat stayed strong in towns with many independent takeaways.

howTheyGetUsers: Wide restaurant choice in smaller towns
growth.moat: Just Eat has a deep list of independent takeaways in UK and European towns, built over 20 years. Many small restaurants list only on Just Eat. Its own-delivery restaurants cost little to serve. But Uber Eats and Deliveroo compete hard in big cities.

northStar.metric: Weekly orders delivered within the promised time and without a complaint
northStar.why: Just Eat's big weakness is that half its orders are delivered by restaurant drivers it does not control. Counting only on-time, complaint-free orders makes the team care about that whole experience, not just order volume, and it grows only when customers and restaurants both win.

improvementIdeas.idea: Show a reliability score for each restaurant's own delivery, based on its last 100 orders, and rank reliable ones higher.
improvementIdeas.problem: Customers blame Just Eat when restaurant drivers are late.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Higher on-time rate and a reason for restaurants to improve.

improvementIdeas.idea: One-tap 'your usual Friday order' suggestion, using Prosus's ordering prediction tools.
improvementIdeas.problem: Order frequency fell for years and lapsed customers drifted away.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More repeat orders from existing customers.

improvementIdeas.idea: Show the full price, with all fees, on the restaurant list rather than at checkout.
improvementIdeas.problem: Fee surprises cause abandoned baskets and complaints.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Higher checkout conversion and fewer fee complaints.

improvementIdeas.idea: Menu health report for independents: which dishes get viewed but not bought, and which get complaints.
improvementIdeas.problem: Small takeaways want more orders but lack data skills.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Better menus and fewer restaurants leaving.

pmLessons: A low-cost marketplace, where restaurants deliver themselves, can be very profitable, but you inherit their quality problems.
Big acquisitions can destroy value. Grubhub cost about $7.3 billion and sold for about $650 million four years later.
Turnarounds take years. Just Eat needed 55 months to get orders growing again.
Running your own delivery wins chains like McDonald's but costs more per order, so mix the two models carefully.

interviewQuestions.question: Why do you think Just Eat's orders fell for 55 months, and how would you reverse it?
interviewQuestions.hint: List causes: the post-COVID drop, Deliveroo and Uber Eats in cities, cutting promotions to save money. Pick the biggest, propose two fixes, and name the metric that shows it worked.

interviewQuestions.question: Marketplace or own delivery: which should Just Eat push?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare cost per order, control over quality and restaurant reach. Conclude it depends on town size and restaurant type, and suggest a rule for choosing.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you grow Just Eat+?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find who orders often but has not joined. Test price points and perks. Track sign-ups, orders per member and whether the fee covers the free delivery cost.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a feature for independent takeaways.
interviewQuestions.hint: Pick one pain: low visibility, poor menus or no data. Suggest a tool, how a restaurant would use it, and measure orders per restaurant and churn.

interviewQuestions.question: You are a PM at Prosus. What would you change in Just Eat's first year?
interviewQuestions.hint: Prioritise by impact: delivery reliability, personalisation, fees. Explain why one comes first and set a 12-month goal.
